title: Hodge mechanism, dimensional reduction, and Habiro placement of the photon IR zero-mode
html:
Remark. Hodge mechanism, dimensional reduction, and Habiro placement of the photon IR zero-mode

Mechanism

The Maxwell sector of the categorical Lagrangian restricts to the UV-completing Bring surface M_4. The surface carries the force-carrier pair \{T_{2,9}, T_{3,5}\} (prop:force-carrier-bring-uniqueness). The zero-momentum two-point function is governed by the kernel of the 1-form Laplacian \Delta_1. By Hodge theory, \dim\ker\Delta_1 = b_1(M_g) = 2g. The heat-kernel zero-mode of a Laplacian contributes one constant mode 1/\mathrm{Vol} per harmonic generator. This yields an infrared shift of b_1/\mathrm{Area}. Gauss–Bonnet fixes the area at curvature -1 to 4\pi(g-1). The resulting infrared shift is 2g/(4\pi(g-1)). It evaluates to 2/(3\pi) at g=4.

Dimensional reduction. A naive attempt places the zero-mode on the 3-manifold M_g\times S^1. Here b_1 = 2g+1 and \mathrm{Vol} = 2\pi\mathrm{Area}. This gives (2g+1)/(8\pi^2(g-1)) = 9/(24\pi^2) \approx 0.038. Crossing with S^1 adds a spurious harmonic generator and a factor of 2\pi to the volume. The photon zero-mode lives strictly on the 2-surface.

Jet-order placement. The Archimedean realisation decomposes into jet grades: \tau = \sum_{n\ge 0} a_D^{(n)} (prop:jet-sw-tau-decomposition). The n=0 term is the electron period. The photon zero-mode forms the n=1 infrared term. This is the first prolongation beyond the tree coupling q[9]_q[10]_q. The n=2 self-energy takes the form \alpha\,[2]_q/(8\pi)\,(1-h^2\alpha). Its denominator depends on the same Hodge datum:

  8\pi \;=\; \pi\cdot\dim H^1(M_{\text{Bring}}) \;=\; \pi\,b_1.

The Betti number b_1 = 8 controls both infrared corrections. The zero-mode carries it in the numerator (b_1/\mathrm{Area}). The self-energy carries it in the denominator (\pi\,b_1). The factors isolate the topological b_1 and the archimedean \pi.

Habiro structure. The n=2 form groups as \alpha\,H(q)/(\pi\,b_1), where H(q) = [2]_q(1-h^2\alpha) is the \alpha_{EM} Habiro element (prop:alpha-em-habiro-bar-involution). Identity 2 acts as the Habiro deformation (1-h^2\alpha). The n=2 self-energy decomposes into three sectors: substrate H, archimedean \pi, and topological b_1. This factorization connects the Hodge realization (b_1/\mathrm{Area}) to the dilogarithm realization via root-of-unity evaluations in the Habiro ring. It indicates a bridge to the Bloch group.
